name: biceps
note: Gym shorthand for the anatomical muscle. Same concept, shorter name.

name: calves
note: Gastrocnemius and soleus together, which is exactly what triceps surae names and exactly what a coach means.

name: chest
note: Close, not exact: a coach's 'chest' also takes in pectoralis minor, which this concept excludes.

name: core
note: Abdominal skeletal muscle is the closest concept SNOMED carries. Pinned rather than searched: ranked search for the phrase returns the abdominal part of pectoralis major, which is a chest muscle.

name: forearms
note: A group rather than a single muscle, and SNOMED models it as one too.

name: glutes
note: SNOMED has no gluteal-group concept — searching for one returns lymph nodes and an accessory-muscle variant. Gluteus maximus is the principal member, so the mapping is narrow and says so rather than pretending to cover medius and minimus.

name: hamstrings
note: Resolves to 'Posterior muscle of thigh structure', which is near-synonymous in practice but drawn on a regional rather than a functional boundary.

name: hip adductors
note: SNOMED locates the group at the hip joint. An earlier query said 'of thigh' and resolved to the group's tendon rather than the muscle — a different tissue, and the kind of near-miss that makes an unchecked mapping worse than none.
snomed_term: Structure of adductor muscle of hip joint

name: hip flexors
note: Iliopsoas is the principal hip flexor, but the training term also carries rectus femoris and sartorius, so the SNOMED concept is the narrower of the two.

name: lats
note: The catalogue's abbreviation of the anatomical name.

name: lower back
note: Deliberately the muscle, not the region. The lumbar-spine reading of 'lower back' is a separate AnatomicalStructure concept mapping to the same SNOMED code by exactMatch — one external concept, two local ones, at two different strengths. That is the ambiguity `decisions.md` Resolver 1 refuses to resolve by precedence.

name: middle back
note: The catalogue's mid-back is chiefly rhomboids, but working middle trapezius too.

name: obliques
note: Pinned to the external oblique. Search alternated between the internal and external oblique across runs, and an unstable clinical mapping is worse than an explicit one. The catalogue's plural covers both, so this is one of two narrow matches and the row shape holds a single mapping.
snomed_term: Structure of external oblique abdominal muscle

name: quads
note: The catalogue's abbreviation of the anatomical name.

name: rotator cuff
note: The same SNOMED concept the AnatomicalStructure of this name maps to — one of the three names claiming two labels, which is why the resolver makes a call site declare which it means.
snomed_term: Structure of rotator cuff including muscles and tendons

name: traps
note: The catalogue's abbreviation of the anatomical name.

name: triceps
note: Gym shorthand for the anatomical muscle.

name: upper back
note: The loosest row in the file, and marked as such. 'Upper back' is a training region with no muscular concept behind it; the nearest SNOMED concept spans the whole back, so it is broader than what the catalogue means.
